title: Desi Twist Brings Upscale Mughlai Cooking to Hoover, Alabama
excerpt: Chef Sanjay Verma's new family-owned restaurant pairs tandoori classics and a halal-certified kitchen with brunch twists like chicken tikka Benedict at Brocks Gap Parkway.
body:
• Desi Twist, an upscale Mughlai Indian restaurant led by Executive Chef Sanjay Verma, has opened at 1031 Brocks Gap Parkway, Suite 151-B, in Hoover, Alabama.
  • The menu pairs tandoori classics and shared plates — tikka masala, Punjabi saag, chicken makhani — with small plates such as Manchurian fire soup, masala okra fries and pasta chaat, plus 10 kinds of breads; the chef's signature is the lamb chops.
  • The kitchen is halal-certified, there is a full-service bar, and weekend brunch runs to chicken tikka Benedict and butter chicken brunch tacos.
  • Hours: closed Mondays; Tuesday-Thursday 3-10 p.m., Friday 3-11 p.m., Saturday and Sunday brunch 11 a.m.-3 p.m. and dinner from 5 p.m. Reservations and details: (205) 593-4034.

Hoover's Indian food scene has a new fine-dining entry. Desi Twist has opened at 1031 Brocks Gap Parkway, near Biscuit Belly and Phil Sandoval's, offering what Bham Now describes as upscale Mughlai cuisine — the slow-cooked, spice-layered cooking that developed over centuries across India, Persia, Afghanistan and Pakistan. The restaurant describes itself as family-owned, and its kitchen is halal-certified.

Executive Chef Sanjay Verma frames the menu as storytelling. "We want everybody to go on a journey with us. Each and every dish has a story. So, if you ask me, what is the name of this dish? Why was this created? And how was it created? I can tell you all about it," Verma told Bham Now. "So, it is about a story and also about a journey."

What is on the menu

The tandoor does the expected heavy lifting — chicken, salmon, shrimp and lamb chops, the last of which is the chef's signature — supported by 10 kinds of breads. The more telling part of the menu is the small plates, where regional cooking meets the Birmingham bar crowd: Manchurian fire soup, masala okra fries, cocktail samosas and pasta chaat. Shared plates stick closer to the canon: tikka masala, Punjabi saag and chicken makhani, and the restaurant's own menu adds a Royal Lamb Shank Nihari, chicken biryani, samosa chaat, palak chaat, tandoori mango shrimp and paneer and dal makhani. Desserts include a Gulab Jamun Volcano and hot jalebi with kulfi.

Weekend brunch is where the "twist" in the name earns its keep: chicken tikka Benedict, chicken tikka and butter chicken brunch tacos, aloo gobi, and masala dosa alongside the Benedict-style dishes. There is a full-service bar and a fine-wine list.

"To the people of Hoover and Birmingham: we're excited to welcome you to Desi Twist. Come with your family, bring your friends, tell us what you enjoy, and be part of what we're building."

— Chef Sanjay Verma

Planning a visit

Desi Twist is at 1031 Brocks Gap Parkway, Suite 151-B, Hoover, AL 35244. It is closed on Mondays, open Tuesday to Thursday from 3 to 10 p.m. and Friday from 3 to 11 p.m.; on Saturdays it serves brunch from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and dinner from 5 to 11 p.m., and on Sundays brunch from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and dinner from 5 to 10 p.m. The restaurant can be reached at (205) 593-4034, and its full menu is on the Desi Twist website. For the Birmingham area's growing Indian community, it adds something the local scene has had less of: a white-tablecloth Mughlai room built for family occasions, not just a takeout counter.
